areas.finding: The named Atlas deer is interpreted as a slender warm-brown live deer with pale throat/belly, short pale-under-tail and modest narrow branching tan antlers. It is distinct from the retained pale Tundra Stag, heavy Giant Elk and equipped companion concepts.

FRONT, LEFT, REAR, RIGHT, FRONT THREE-QUARTER and REAR THREE-QUARTER are distinct, correctly directed and complete. Side profiles oppose each other and obliques expose body depth and appendage attachment.

Two attached branching antlers retain the same narrow beam-and-tine architecture through the six views. Front/rear show matching major forks; side and oblique overlap is consistent with perspective. Native antler crops inspected for every view.
Four deer legs are resolved through profiles and obliques, with cloven hooves, sensible hock/knee direction and floor contact. Frontal/rear self-occlusion does not create extra or missing limbs.
Two ears, dark nose/eyes, pale muzzle/throat/belly and one short tail remain coherent. Rear and oblique views clearly show the tail attached to the rump with pale underside.
Slender neck/limbs, ordinary deer body mass and short fur remain consistent across rotations; no heavy elk mane, giant hostile enlargement or companion equipment appears.
Polished sculpted fur masses, expressive face and soft studio grounding fit Havenline. Every antler tip, hoof and tail remains in frame; no snowbank obscures anatomy.

source_interpretation_limit: Original Atlas provides one very small pose. Reverse surfaces, precise fur grouping and hidden three-dimensional branching are authored reference interpretation; no canonical anatomy beyond the source appearance and no native mesh/rig proof is asserted.
minor_polish_limit: Small fur-tuft grouping and tine thickness vary illustratively with view. Source-specific silhouette, major appendages, anatomy and view coverage remain clear.
family_static_reference_status: Six-view dedicated Atlas deer sheet passes; this does not replace or rename an earlier approved animal.
